title: Atoma — the supervision loop
purpose: A 12-second motion-design test that makes delegation, evidence checking and correction understandable without technical knowledge.

delivery.export: MP4 through the editor if MCP export is unavailable

visualDirection.typography: Inter, with short sentence-case labels and tabular timing labels only where useful
visualDirection.composition: Three stable horizontal levels in one continuous shot; large readable nodes, restrained depth, fine connectors. Keep role names and positions stable throughout.
visualDirection.motion: Task cards visibly move down; results and evidence visibly move up. Emphasize one active relationship at a time. Use a single coral return path for correction. Use purposeful easing and holds, with no camera orbit or decorative particle field.
visualDirection.brandReference: Colors follow src/viz/client-gl/brand-mark.ts: tissue violet, cell amber, molecule teal, with lighter shades for contrast on the dark background.

roles.label: Plan
roles.responsibility: Decompose the goal and review phase outcomes

roles.label: Supervise
roles.responsibility: Delegate work and validate plans and results

roles.label: Execute
roles.responsibility: Use tools and produce deliverables and evidence

beats.action: Reveal the three stable levels and one objective card. Keep the objective generic: Build a deliverable. The L3 card sends a phase to L2.
L2 selects one of three L1 workers. A small Route checkpoint lights on the handoff. The task card follows the connector to the selected worker; the other workers remain quiet.
beats.caption: Delegate

beats.action: The selected L1 worker invokes a small tool row beneath it. A file card is produced and moves upward to L2.
beats.caption: Execute

beats.action: A check panel beside L2 reads Evidence missing. Hold the reason long enough to read. The upper-level phase stays pending. Send the same task card back down a coral return path, labelled Verify output.
beats.caption: Check

beats.action: The worker performs the requested verification. Attach a distinct evidence chip to the file card; do not merely recolor the original file. Return the file and evidence to L2.
beats.caption: Improve

beats.action: L2 now shows Checks passed. The verified phase result moves upward to L3, whose status becomes Review deliverable. Do not imply that an intermediate approval is final acceptance or deployment.
Hold the complete three-level composition, with the correction loop still legible but subdued. Show the concluding line Supervision at every handoff.
beats.caption: Supervision at every handoff.

architectureConstraints: There are three agent tiers. Tools are not a fourth agent tier.
Both supervisory levels use the plan, validate, execute, validate protocol. This short test focuses on one result-checking loop.
Decision checkpoints are bounded routing or intermediate approval decisions, not a fourth tier and not root delivery acceptance.
An uncertain decision defers to model review. A Decision refusal alone does not reject the child; model validation owns that judgment.
The example correction is explanatory, not a claim that a specific production run exhibited these exact events.
Do not display production metrics, invented trace events, project secrets, Attica application UI, xe.gr, or the underlying decision-provider name.
The full film will connect this conceptual sequence to verified production evidence from atoma.run.
qualityChecks: At normal playback, a first-time viewer can identify who delegates, who executes, and who checks.
The correction has a readable cause and the subsequent evidence visibly resolves it.
All primary labels remain readable at a 960-by-540 playback size.
No clipped text, overlapping cards, unexplained parallel work or ambiguous connector direction.
Source elements and timing remain editable in Jitter.
voiceoverCandidate: Atoma delegates the work, checks the evidence, and sends incomplete results back for correction. Every handoff has supervision.
